### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ff2526dd03ba3ff39ca2465aa75579edb894914` — the merge of head `d7ef4bd6d72fa79e16feb86a0417b56a5a8bda1c` into base `394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ff2526dd03ba3ff39ca2465aa75579edb894914 && git checkout 4ff2526dd03ba3ff39ca2465aa75579edb894914
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 d7ef4bd6d72fa79e16feb86a0417b56a5a8bda1c && git checkout -B drift-repro 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 && git merge --no-ff d7ef4bd6d72fa79e16feb86a0417b56a5a8bda1c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `66b826f9d9b159bfaf180fc8abde3cde44ec0f16`
Local-runs: none

Read: the net diff `origin/main...66b826f9d9` (6 files, +357/−10; merge base `5656c5638a`, and main has not touched these files since), the PR body, card comments 6162365516, 6163669810, 6163356782, 6164220398, 6164948359, ruling 6163114098, pointer 6158876765, ADR-0131 D10 on `origin/main`, and the head's check-runs, last read at 2026-10-14T09:37Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Every test verdict below comes from reading the code, except the CI conclusions quoted.

### ① Derived judgments

**F1 (must fix): a test on `main` that this PR leaves untouched now fails.** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.fate-supplement.integration.test.ts` came with #23348 and is in the CI-mandatory integration tier. Two of its cases run `--apply --backup-taken` without `--plan-file`:
- `with --fate-supplement, the apply step receives the host row` (line 147);
- `control: without it, the apply step is handed no inventory` (line 155).

At this head, `runApply` refuses `plan-file-required` before the boot and before `applyOrganizationOwnership`. So `toMatchObject({ report: … })` and `expect(apply).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` both fail. The dev's 33/33 covered two files only, not this one.

CI agrees. `Test Core (3/6)` failed at step 12 ("Run this shard's tests"), and its annotation reads `packages/cli … pnpm run test exited (1)`. The required `Test Core` context failed with it. The failing case's name is not readable here: the proxy refused the job-log download. The failure is consistent with these two cases.

Remedy: give both cases a plan-shaped `--plan-file`. The apply is mocked there, so only the parse runs.

**F2 (must fix, or the seat rules the narrower claim): the posture changes what the apply does, and it is neither in the digest nor compared.**
- The plan file records `posture`. `reviewedPlanFromFile` reads only `generatedAt`, `database` and `inventoryDigest`.
- The posture comes from `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` / `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED` and is resolved separately on each run.
- Under `single` with a Default Organization, attribution gives every anchorless NULL row to that organization (organization-ownership-plan.ts, about line 811). That includes every application table, because `APPLICATION_OBJECT_FATE` is `attribution` with no anchors. Under `isolated`/`group` those rows are reported (fate 4, "never guessed").
- `authored-conversion` converts organization-authored sets and positions only under `single`; under a wall it reports them (apply.ts line 572).
- So a plan reviewed under `isolated`, which lists rows as reported, can be applied under `single`, which writes owners for them. Plan A runs as plan B through one environment variable, and the changeset's "executes only the plan the operator reviewed" does not hold.
- Remedy: compare `posture` (for example `plan-posture-mismatch`), with a pin and its ablation.

Other inputs outside the digest:
- `--template-choice`: apply-only by design. The plan lists each conflict and the operator chooses at apply, under 6020178017.
- The database's state between plan and apply (new rows, a new application table, a Default Organization created in between): D10 does not bind it, so it is not this stage's to bind.
- The ceremony's code: the digest covers the inventory, not the steps. A later release's CLI with an unchanged inventory accepts an earlier plan file. `ceremonyVersion` is in the file but not compared, so "another release" is caught only when the inventory moved. Not blocking.

**Unreviewed plans: what is refused, and when.**
- Refused before the backup question and before the boot, pinned with `boot` not called: no flag (`plan-file-required`), a missing file, not JSON, an apply report, an empty digest, a missing database (`plan-file-unusable`). `--plan-file` without `--apply` is refused as `flag-without-apply`.
- Digest and database mismatch are refused after the backup question and after the served boot, as the PR says. They are refused before the ledger read, before `validateTemplateChoices`, before every step, and so before mirror-deletion's gate re-read and before any UPDATE, DELETE or DDL. `planFor` issues SELECT only.
- Weakness (not blocking): `inventoryDigest(inventory)` is a pure function of the merged inventory, which `runApply` already holds. The digest refusal could come before the backup question and the boot. As built, the operator confirms a backup for an apply that will be refused, and a boot failure hides the mismatch. The claim that nothing is written before the refusal rests on the one-shot boot's no-write design. The dogfood measured `sys_migration` ceremony rows, not whole-database identity.
- Weakness (not blocking): `plan-database-mismatch` compares `stack.dbLabel`, a display string (`describeDb`: a DSN with credentials and query string stripped, a SQLite filename as written, or the client name when the config carries no address). It can wrongly accept two databases that differ only in the query string, two configs without an address, or a relative SQLite path resolved from another directory. The module's own `describeDriverSqliteFile` warns against reading identity off this string.

**Checkpoint under another digest.** A checkpoint is reused only when its digest equals the current digest, and after the refusal the current digest is the reviewed one. A checkpoint under another digest yields `completed: {}`, so no step the reviewed plan names is skipped. It is reported in `restartedFrom` (the `superseded` list) and announced by `onProgress`.

**The refusal.** It names the file and both digests (or both database labels), says that nothing was written, and gives the remedy (plan again with the same flags, review, pass the new file). Reason codes are stable, the `--json` error is `apply_refused`, and the exit code is 1. Gap: the command-level mapping of a `ReviewedPlanRefusal` raised after the boot (the catch branch in `runApply`) is pinned by no test. If that branch were removed, the refusal would surface as `apply_failed` with "re-run --apply to resume". Only the dogfood observed the mapping.

**Do the tests fail when the comparison is removed?**
- The ablation turned `refuseUnreviewedPlan` into a no-op, and both mismatch pins failed. That covers the database path too, since both checks live in that one function.
- The checkpoint-supersede path was not ablated. By reading, its pin fails if `restartedFrom` is dropped (`toEqual`), or if a checkpoint under a foreign digest is reused (`resumedFrom` would be non-empty and `attribution` would read `checkpointed`).

**What on `main` invokes `--apply` without `--plan-file`:**
- F1, above.
- **F3 (must fix):** `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts` line 204 declares `--apply --backup-taken …` as this command's write mode. It is now refused before the boot, so the #21391 "a write mode runs no seed write" pin and the #21471 key-material pin pass without testing anything for this command. Nothing fails; the coverage is simply gone. Give that mode a plan file so it boots again.
- F4 is under ②.
- `content/docs` (`capabilities.mdx`, `permission-sets.mdx`) only mentions `--apply` in prose, which stays true. The CLI examples are updated.
- Stale, not blocking: the module doc's "It asks about the backup first", and the oclif `description` does not mention the plan file.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` with `Clause-②: no` is correct by the WHICH LEVEL rule.** The command's released surface (18.0.0-next.0, CHANGELOG `cc305a3`) is the plan mode only. `22937-*` and `23280-*` are still pending in `.changeset/`, not in `.changeset/pre/`.
- `--plan-file` is refused outside the unreleased `--apply`, so no released invocation accepts a new key or loses one.
- `reviewedPlan` and `restartedFrom` sit on the unreleased apply report, and the plan payload is unchanged.
- The narrowing lands inside #22937's pending `minor` release (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`), so the combined level is unchanged.
- **Q-S4 → A, as applied:** the corrected example (`--apply --backup-taken --plan-file plan.json`) is accurate, and it runs as written at this head. Minor: the note's "The backup comes first" bullet now trails the plan-file refusal.
- **Check Changeset fails only for the correction.** In both runs only step 12 (`Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR`) failed. Its one failure annotation names `.changeset/22937-cli-organization-ownership-apply.md` as a deliberate correction. ADR-0087 (step 13) and the major/level guard (step 15) are green.
- **F4 (seat decision): the same defect in another note.** `.changeset/23280-host-fate-supplement.md` line 20 is pending and `minor`: `os migrate organization-ownership --fate-supplement host-fates.json --apply --backup-taken`. At this head that invocation is refused as `plan-file-required`, so the compiled CHANGELOG would print it, which is the reason given for Q-S4 A. The seat's answer named #22937's note only. Either extend A to this note, with the confirmation on the PR, or rule otherwise.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation, `--plan-file` instead of `--plan FILE`:** accepted. D10 item 1 names the bare read-only mode `--plan`. The ADR does not yet record the plan-file precondition of D10 item 3; that ADR text belongs to #23403, not here.
- **Deviation, the #22937 note reverted and then corrected:** answered by 6164948359 and stated in the PR body. The seat's on-PR confirmation is still owed at ACCEPT.
- **Q-S4:** answered A. F4 extends the same question to #23280's note, unanswered.
- **Dispatch item 4:** no acknowledgement flag exists or is needed, and the refusal is loud with no silent re-plan. Met, except for F2's posture route.
- **Out-of-scope finding, escalated (carrier: the seat):** on a freshly seeded showcase database, `rewrite` stops on `admin_full_access` and `organization_admin_no_bypass`, which the ceremony's security catalog does not resolve. The diff does not touch it; it has not been re-run on bare `main`, and it needs a card.
- **NOT MEASURED by the dev, but measured by CI on this head:** the dev's 5 exit-3 gates all passed.
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape` (Lint · CI, release & engine gates, step 53);
  - `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:i18n-walk-parity` (Type Check · consumer gates, steps 26–28);
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (Build Core, step 15).
- **Gate verdicts on the head, all completed at 2026-10-14T09:37Z, none still running:**
  - `Test Core` (a required context) failed, because `Test Core (3/6)` failed in the `packages/cli` suite (F1). Shards 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 passed.
  - `Check Changeset` failed twice, by design (②).
- **Not measured by anyone:**
  - the posture-mismatch route (F2);
  - `plan-database-mismatch` and checkpoint supersede through the real binary;
  - whole-database identity after a digest refusal;
  - the name of the case that failed in shard 3/6 (the job log could not be read);
  - F3's file passes in CI, which is exactly the problem: it passes without testing the apply.
- Every other check-run on the head passed or was skipped.

**Seat adoption** (2026-10-14T09:39Z). Adopted after an audit of the reviewer transcript: one Write, to this record only; 70 Bash calls, all reads (`git show`, `git diff`, `git ls-tree`, REST GETs); no MCP call, no GitHub write, no worktree, build or test run. The seat re-read F1 on `origin/main` (the two cases at lines 147 and 155 of the fate-supplement integration test call `--apply --backup-taken` with no plan file) and F4 (`.changeset/23280-host-fate-supplement.md:20`). The seat rules:
- **F1, F2, F3:** fix in this PR. F2 compares the plan file's recorded posture against the running posture and refuses on a mismatch, with a pin and an ablation.
- **F4:** Q-S4 → A extends to this note too (the same class: a wording correction of an unreleased note). The PR body names both corrected sentences.
- **Non-blocking:** the stale wording (the module doc, the #22937 note's backup sentence) rides this patch. The rest stays as noted.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-15211-c7b-plan-digest`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0802a12756f042750737f571072111c396702f24`
Local-runs: none

Delta review against the FAIL record 6165431301 (head `66b826f9d9`). The head has not moved since the brief. Read: the delta `66b826f9d9..0802a12756` (one commit, 9 files, +130/−30), the net diff from merge base `5656c5638a` (9 files, +474/−27), the PR body, the dev report 6167752569, the seat answer 6164948359, and the head's check-runs, last read at 2026-10-14T12:04Z. To judge "any other test on `main`" and the semver premise, I also read current `main` (`cb9841aa25`) and a local `git merge-tree` of it with the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Every test verdict below comes from reading the code, except where a dev measurement is quoted.

### ① Derived judgments

**F1, as ruled: fixed.** In `organization-ownership.fate-supplement.integration.test.ts`, both `--apply` cases now pass `--plan-file` (`writePlan()`, a plan-shaped file that includes `posture`). Each keeps its pin: the host row reaches the mocked apply, and the control case is handed no `inventory`. The supplement-refusal case at line 205 still runs `--apply` without a plan file, which is correct: the supplement refusal fires in `run()` before `runApply`.

**F5 (must fix): `main` moved, and two newer tests on `main` run the apply without a reviewed plan.** The merge with `main` has no textual conflicts, so both tests land in the merged tree, and the merged tree breaks them:
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-not-declared.integration.test.ts` (#23446, merged 2026-10-14T09:28Z). Line 114 runs the real command `--apply --backup-taken` with no `--plan-file`, and it asserts `payload.error` is undefined. With this PR the run is refused as `plan-file-required`, so cases (i) and (ii) fail.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.served-catalog.integration.test.ts` (#23433, merged 2026-10-14T09:41Z). Line 121 calls `applyOrganizationOwnership` with no `reviewedPlan`:
  - at runtime, `refuseUnreviewedPlan(run.plan, opts.reviewedPlan)` reads `inventoryDigest` off `undefined`, so the `single` and `walled` cases throw a TypeError;
  - `reviewedPlan` is required in `ApplyOptions`, and `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` includes all of `src`, so by reading the cli `tsc --noEmit` also fails.

Nothing else invokes this command's `--apply` without a plan file:
- In `packages/` and `examples/` of the merged tree, the only other cases are the deliberate `plan-file-required` pin and the supplement-refusal case.
- `content/docs/**` mentions the command only in prose (`capabilities.mdx`, `permission-sets.mdx`), and that prose stays true.

Remedy: merge `main`, then give the first test a plan run and its file, and give the second test a `reviewedPlan`.

**F2: fixed.**
- `refuseUnreviewedPlan` compares `reviewed.posture` with `plan.posture` after the SELECT-only `planFor`. That is before `validateTemplateChoices`, the ledger read, and every step.
- The refusal is `plan-posture-mismatch`. It names both values, says that nothing was written, and gives both remedies: apply under the plan's posture, or plan again.
- The pin `refuses, before any write, a plan computed under another tenancy posture` asserts no writes, no checkpoint, and an unchanged database hash. By reading, it goes red without the comparison, because the digest and database match, so the apply would proceed. The dev measured that ablation red.
- **Same source:** both modes call `resolveTenancyPosture()` once in `run()`, before branching:
  - the plan run writes that value as `plan.posture`;
  - the apply passes the same value as `opts.posture`, which both `planFor` and the authored-conversion step read;
  - so the env vars are the same (`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE`, else `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED` true means `isolated`, else `single`), and both sides compare the normalized value, with `multi` normalized to `isolated`.
- A plan file without `posture` is refused as `plan-file-unusable`, before the backup question and the boot. It is pinned.
- Still not compared: `ceremonyVersion`. It is the literal `1` on both sides, so comparing it would catch nothing until it is bumped. Non-blocking, as the baseline found. `client` follows the database label. I found no other recorded input that adds actions. Composition and catalog differences can only block a step, as #23446's not-declared shows.
- Like the digest refusal, the posture refusal still comes after the backup question and the boot (the baseline's non-blocking weakness, which the dev did not change).

**F3: fixed.**
- The one-shot family's `--apply` mode declares `after`: a plan run that writes the reviewed file. `runBefore` asserts that run returned no error.
- The #21391 write pin now asserts that the apply's own payload has no `error`. So it reaches the boot and the real `applyOrganizationOwnership`, and the seed pin tests this command again. The guard against a vacuous pass is sound.
- The #21471 pin reaches the boot too: once the preceding run has written a valid file, no refusal before the boot remains. Minor, non-blocking: like every mode, it asserts only that the error is not `boot_failed`, not that the apply reached its write.
- Measured locally by the dev (88/88), not by CI (③).

**F4 and the riders, as worded: correct. As a remedy: overtaken (see ②).**
- Both notes' examples now carry `--plan-file plan.json`. The #22937 bullet now says the plan file comes before the backup question, and that is accurate.
- The PR body names both corrected sentences.
- The stale wording is fixed: the module doc, the oclif `description`, and the #22937 backup bullet.
- The new mapping pin is sound. By reading, removing the `ReviewedPlanRefusal` catch branch sends the refusal to `apply-failed`, which emits `error: apply_failed`, and the pin's `toMatchObject` with `apply_refused`, its reason and both values goes red. The dev measured that ablation red.

**Carried to S1 (#23452), not a FAIL here:** `--template-choice` deletions come from groups recomputed at apply time.
- The report (out-of-scope item 1) describes the gap honestly. It leaves the placement to the seat and does not name #23452.
- The PR body names neither the gap nor its carrier.
- S4 overclaims nothing in substance: the note lists exactly three comparisons. But the headline "executes only the plan the operator reviewed" is unqualified.
- Rider: one line in the PR body naming #23452 as the carrier.

### ② Semver level

**F6 (must fix, seat ruling): the premise behind `patch` / `Clause-②: no` has failed on `main`. `--apply` has shipped.**
- The version commit `0c52e43075` (#23382, 2026-10-14T10:19Z) consumed `22937-cli-organization-ownership-apply.md` and `23280-host-fate-supplement.md` into `.changeset/pre/`.
- `packages/cli` is now `18.0.0-next.1`, and its CHANGELOG prints both bare invocations at lines 44 and 60: `--apply --backup-taken` and `--fate-supplement host-fates.json --apply --backup-taken`.
- github-actions pushed the tag `@objectstack/cli@18.0.0-next.1` at 2026-10-14T11:58Z. Release run 38551831636 was in its "Publish to npm + push version tags" step at 2026-10-14T12:00Z.

What follows:
- The changeset's "`--apply` has not shipped in a release yet (its changeset is still pending), so no released invocation changes" is false, and so is the PR body's matching acceptance note.
- On the released surface, this PR adds a new accepted flag (`--plan-file`), new keys on the apply report (`reviewedPlan`, `restartedFrom`), and new reason values. The delta's `plan-posture-mismatch` and its posture requirement add to these. Together they are a widening. By WHICH LEVEL that means at least `minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
- The PR also refuses the released invocation `--apply --backup-taken`. That is a narrowing. In the launch window, that kind of break is carried by the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level.
- The baseline's "the narrowing lands inside #22937's pending `minor`" no longer holds.
- The seat rules the level, the declaration and the banner. The PR's own note must then say that the released bare invocation is now refused.

**F4 re-opened by F6.**
- Q-S4 A's class, "a wording correction of an unreleased note", no longer applies.
- In the merged tree the two edits land on `.changeset/pre/22937-…` and `.changeset/pre/23280-…`, which are consumed notes. They change nothing in the published `18.0.0-next.1` CHANGELOG.
- Seat decision: keep or revert those edits, and carry the correction in this PR's own note instead.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Gate verdicts on the head: none exist.**
  - At 2026-10-14T12:04Z, `0802a12756` had 0 check-runs and 0 workflow runs. Five check suites (vercel, fly-io, claude, cloudflare-workers-and-pages, objectstack-fleet) were queued, with no runs.
  - GitHub reports the PR `mergeable: false` and `mergeable_state: dirty`.
  - `refs/pull/23437/merge` is still `9aa1106aa7`, the merge of the previous head `66b826f9d9`.
  - So nothing failed and nothing is running, but nothing is measured. That includes `Test Core`, which was red at the baseline over F1, and `Check Changeset`.
- **Dev deviation, "Main was not merged (the push did not conflict)":** that was true locally, for the text only. GitHub says the PR is dirty, and the merged tree breaks the two tests (F5).
- **Dev claims not measured by CI:** 1,105/0/2 for the integration tier, 83/83, 88/88, typecheck 0, the two new ablations, dispatch-gates at 65 of 65, and `check:query-options-erasure` red once (attributed to a race) and then exit 0 when run alone.
- **Out-of-scope 1** (`--template-choice` binding): carried to S1 (#23452) by the seat (①).
- **Out-of-scope 2** (the digest and posture refusals could come before the boot; the database comparison reads the display label): left undone, as the baseline's non-blocking grading allows.
- **The showcase `rewrite` stop** on `admin_full_access` and `organization_admin_no_bypass` is reported on the card (6163356782). Since then, #23433 on `main` touches how the ceremony resolves built-in positions. Whether that bears on the stop is not measured.
- **Not measured by anyone:**
  - every CI gate on this head;
  - the posture route through the real binary;
  - the merged tree's four failing cases and the `tsc` failure, which come from reading only;
